title: How to Win My Heart
essence: The poet walks down from the white temple to a corner café on the harbor of the heavens and sits at a small table, watching couples, while the tide comes in under the boats. Dusk counts out Jupiter's moons over the water; his younger self watches from the rail, the elders pray with their pearls, and his love letters burn on the quay stones. He harvests a field of scarlet poppies and purple blossoms until it flowers out of his own arms, and then, across the water, a distant window comes into focus with a woman in it, and he takes off his sunglasses and says hello.
palette_notes: Bay blue #465fb1 is the poem's colour in film/poems.json and the dusk sky over the harbor; harbor teal #0f5f63 and night navy #10243f are the water under the boardwalk and the night pier (932cb5b5_2, 3238a164_1, fc83bfee_0). Lantern gold #f0a64a is the café's string lights and paper lanterns (22ddf809_2, 932cb5b5_2). Quay grey #5c6670 is wet stone. The two flower colours are the accents: scarlet poppy #c8231e and purple blossom #7a3fa0, and SHE's red dress takes the poppy scarlet so the field and the window rhyme. Linen cream #e9dcc4 is the couples' summer clothes and the letters.

full_text.line: I want you to notice me in a corner cafe
at the Harbor of the Heavens, wandering in thought,
discovering water on Jupiter's moons,
healing the sick with silent prayers
and molding a better world to return to
with every pulsing beat after walking alone.
I want you to really notice me
with the distances we couldn't avoid
and our younger selves watching and dreaming,
while our elders clutch their pearls,
hold their faith and breath closely,
freeing their worries peacefully.
I've journeyed beyond any place you can conceivably be.
So I thought, life has burned all of my love stories.
All ends led to losses,
victory-less seasons for a man that wanted just one win.
I could celebrate forever.
Ice has frozen and thawed
friendships in death and departure.
I've learned to love myself more,
manage loss and harvest a wizardry more brilliant
than the scarlet poppies and purple blossoms
that time and tears have disclaimed.
Yet from a distant window, beautiful and calm,
hope tells me you'll see me.
And if you notice me and capture my eyes
as you refocus yours,
stepping back and letting them say hello,
all the fatigue of wandering alone in thought,
in winless seasons and scarlet poppies
won't prevent me from sharing a smile
worth the promise of my heart.

insights: One quantity per movement and it only goes one way: tide in, dark down, smoke up, field down, focus in. Pick the object that shows each number and never let it turn round.
Build the harbor as one tonal pass (sky, mud, water, quay) so day, dusk and night are the same set relit, and the tide is a moving line, not a redrawn object.
SHE is tiny and far: give her a dedicated small-scale head and keep her eyes to seven points; at full puppet scale she will read as a doll.
The becoming must stay HIS body with flowers growing out of it; a torso-and-stems substitute reads as a scarecrow.
The red of her dress is the poppy red: the field he harvests and the woman he hopes for are the same colour.

Transcript corrections from the treatment: 'Ice has frozen in thought' is 'Ice has frozen and thawed friendships'; 'at time and tears have just claimed' is 'that time and tears have disclaimed'; 'windless seasons' is 'winless seasons'.
future: The harbor, the temple on its rise and the boats are what the haze takes first in 14.
The poppy field is the 'field' card in 14's reel.
The couples-in-orbit move becomes 14's two entwined muses (the same turn, both him).
The window motif closes here as a window that looks back; in 14 the window stays shut and he chooses a door.
